lines.text: A refinery can make useful saturated hydrocarbons in two different ways. The starting molecule tells you which route is available.

Hydrogenation adds H two gas across an alkene C equals C bond to produce an alkane. Use a platinum or nickel catalyst and heat, for example, C two H four plus H two yields C two H six. Cracking instead breaks a longer chain alkane into smaller molecules by heating it with ay L two O three. A shorter alkane may be one of the products, often alongside an alkene. Balance carbon and hydrogen atoms in every proposed equation.
Hydrogenation removes unsaturation by addition. Cracking changes chain length and is also a route from a heavy fraction to smaller molecules.
Alkene plus H two gas gives alkane, platinum or nickel catalyst, heat. Long chain alkane gives smaller hydrocarbons, heat with ay L two O three.
How could you distinguish alkene hydrogenation from alkane cracking by reagents and conditions?
The oxygen supply and the presence of ultraviolet light determine two very different sets of alkane products.

In complete combustion, an alkane reacts with sufficient oxygen to form C O two and H two O. In limited oxygen, incomplete combustion can make C O or carbon, soot, as well as water. Ethane undergoes free radical substitution with C L two or B R two in ultraviolet light, one H atom is replaced by a halogen atom. The first chlorination gives C two H five C L and H C L, the first bromination gives C two H five B R and H B R. Further substitution can occur, giving a mixture when halogen is in excess.
Combustion oxidises the carbon skeleton. Halogen substitution preserves it while replacing C H with C halogen.
Complete combustion, C O two and H two O. Incomplete combustion, C O and or or soot, plus water. Ethane plus C L two or B R two, U V, free radical substitution.
Why can the same alkane give either carbon dioxide or carbon monoxide on burning?
A radical chain reaction continues because each propagation cycle makes a new radical. Tracking radicals identifies every stage.

Initiation, ultraviolet light breaks the halogen halogen bond homolytically, C L two yields two chlorine radical. Each atom takes one bonding electron. Propagation in ethane chlorination, chlorine radical plus C two H six yields H C L plus C two H five radical, then C two H five radical plus C L two yields C two H five C L plus chlorine radical. A radical is used and another appears, continuing the chain. Termination, two radicals combine so no radical remains, such as C two H five radical plus chlorine radical yields C two H five C L or two C two H five radical yields C four H ten. The same pattern applies with bromine.
This mechanism explains why ultraviolet light is needed and why multiple substituted products can appear.
Initiation, homolytic fission under U V makes radicals. Propagation, one radical consumed, one regenerated. Termination, radicals combine, none remains.
A step begins with two radicals and ends with a molecule. Which stage is it, and why?
Fractional distillation can leave too much heavy hydrocarbon fraction and too little of the smaller molecules people need.

Cracking breaks larger molecules in heavier crude oil fractions into smaller hydrocarbons. Heating with ay L two O three is a route for cracking a long chain alkane. It supplies lower M r alkanes, useful as fuels, and lower M r alkenes, useful as feedstocks for reactions such as polymerisation. A balanced example is C ten H twenty two yields C eight H eighteen plus C two H four. The products must together contain exactly the starting numbers of carbon and hydrogen atoms.
The products of cracking include an alkene, which can itself be hydrogenated to an alkane under the conditions of the previous outcome.
Heavy fraction, longer chain, higher M r hydrocarbons. Cracking gives useful lower M r alkanes and alkenes. Check atom balance in a suggested equation.
Why would a refinery crack a heavy fraction even if it already contains combustible hydrocarbons?
Many polar reagents react quickly with functional groups, yet an alkane usually resists them. Its C H bond explains why.

Alkanes are generally unreactive, including towards polar reagents. Their C H bonds are strong, so bond breaking requires substantial energy. The bonds also have relatively little polarity because carbon and hydrogen have a small electronegativity difference. There is no strongly charged site on the alkane for a polar reagent to attack readily. These are two separate reasons, strength concerns the energy needed to break a bond, while polarity concerns charge separation and attraction to a reagent.
UV initiated halogen substitution works by making highly reactive radicals first, despite this usual resistance to polar reagents.
C H bonds are strong, substantial energy is needed to break them. C H bonds are relatively non polar, polar reagents have no strongly charged site to attack.
What does bond strength explain, and what does lack of bond polarity explain?
An engine may burn fuel but still emit harmful gases and unburnt hydrocarbons. The converter has a separate task for each.

Alkane combustion in an internal combustion engine can release carbon monoxide from incomplete combustion, oxides of nitrogen formed at high engine temperatures, and unburnt hydrocarbons. Carbon monoxide is poisonous because it reduces blood oxygen transport. Nitrogen oxides and unburnt hydrocarbons contribute to photochemical smog, nitrogen oxides can also contribute to acid rain. A catalytic converter oxidises C O to C O two and unburnt hydrocarbons to C O two and H two O, while reducing nitrogen oxides to N two. For example, two C O plus two N O yields two C O two plus N two. It reduces these pollutants but still releases carbon dioxide.
Incomplete combustion explains one exhaust pollutant, the converter then changes it chemically before release.
C O, poisonous, reduces oxygen transport. Nitrogen oxides and unburnt hydrocarbons, photochemical smog. Converter, oxidises C O and hydrocarbons, reduces nitrogen oxides to N two.
For C O, nitrogen oxides and unburnt hydrocarbons, what are their converter products?

Light breaks C L two homolytically into radicals, not ions as C claims. The correct option is B.

A abstracts hydrogen from chloroethane and leaves another radical, so it is propagation. D combines radicals and terminates the chain. The correct option is ay.

Alkanes undergo free radical substitution with halogens in U V light. Electrophilic substitution is not their characteristic reaction. The correct option is C.

Both steps regenerate a radical and propagate the chain. B mislabels the second step termination even though a radical remains. The correct option is D.

Which reaction occurs when ethane and chlorine are mixed in diffused sunlight?
Ethane and chlorine undergo UV initiated free radical substitution, giving chloroethane and H C L. Hydrogen gas is not produced. The correct option is B.

All gas volumes were measured at the same temperature and pressure. Which volume of gas was absorbed by the alkali?
Each methane volume gives one C O two volume, each ethane volume gives two. Thus ten plus twenty equals thirty cubic centimetres is absorbed, B omits methane's contribution. The correct option is C.

Water formation needs three oxygen atoms per ethane, so one point five moles O two. C is the complete combustion requirement to C O two and water. The correct option is ay.

The ten carbon alkane is C ten H twenty two, leaving sixteen minus ten equals six carbon atoms and thirty four minus twenty two equals twelve hydrogen atoms for C six H twelve. Thus C sixteen H thirty four yields C ten H twenty two plus C six H twelve conserves sixteen coulombs atoms and thirty four henries atoms, the products are a shorter alkane and an alkene.

A student proposes C fourteen H thirty yields C eight H eighteen plus C six H fourteen as a cracking equation. Suggest whether the products conserve atoms and have lower M r than the feedstock. Carbon balances, but the products contain eighteen plus fourteen equals thirty two H atoms instead of thirty, lower molecular masses alone do not make the proposal valid. The corrected equation is C fourteen H thirty yields C eight H eighteen plus C six H twelve, with eight plus six equals fourteen C and eighteen plus twelve equals thirty H atoms, using A r open bracket C close bracket equals twelve and A r open bracket H close bracket equals one, the proposed products have M r equals one hundred and fourteen and eighty six, both below one hundred and ninety eight, and the corrected alkene has M r equals eighty four. The alkane is useful as a fuel and the alkene as a feedstock for polymerisation.

Count each element on each side before deciding whether the proposal works.

Strong C H bonds require substantial energy to break. Their relative lack of polarity means little charge separation, so there is no strongly charged site for a polar reagent to attack readily.
Consider both the energy of bond breaking and the charge distribution.

Relate electronegativity difference to the attraction of a polar reagent.
Which statement best explains why alkanes resist attack by polar reagents?

Bond strength concerns the energy needed to break a bond, while bond polarity concerns charge separation. Strong, relatively non polar C H bonds explain the resistance, weak bonds, strongly charged sites, or saturation alone do not provide both reasons.
Separate bond strength from bond polarity.
Ask which property controls bond breaking energy and which controls charge separation.
A saturated formula alone says nothing about the energy needed to break a particular bond.

Carbon containing pollutants undergo oxidation, while nitrogen oxides undergo reduction.

Complete combustion in the engine already produces C O two, and oxidation of C O and unburnt hydrocarbons in the converter produces more. The converter does not remove all carbon dioxide, reducing toxic pollutants does not eliminate greenhouse gas emissions.
Track the carbon atoms through the engine and converter.

Alkanes are saturated hydrocarbons whose strong, relatively non polar C H bonds make them generally unreactive, especially towards polar reagents. Heat can crack large hydrocarbons into useful smaller molecules, combustion and UV initiated halogen substitution are the main reactions to know.
Key ideas.

Making alkanes. Hydrogenation adds H two gas across an alkene's C equals C bond with a platinum or nickel catalyst and heat. For example, C two H four gas plus H two gas yields C two H six gas. Cracking a longer chain alkane by heating it with ay L two O three can also make a shorter alkane. Both atoms and bonds must balance in a proposed cracking equation.

Combustion. In enough oxygen, complete combustion gives carbon dioxide and water, two C two H six gas plus seven O two gas yields four C O two gas plus six H two O gas. With limited oxygen, incomplete combustion can produce toxic carbon monoxide or solid carbon, soot, as well as water. For example, two C two H six gas plus five O two gas yields four C O gas plus six H two O gas. The carbon monoxide equation uses five oxygen molecules, so check oxygen atoms as well as carbon and hydrogen.

Halogen substitution. Ethane reacts with C L two or B R two in ultraviolet light. A hydrogen is replaced by halogen, C two H six plus C L two yields C two H five C L plus H C L. Further substitution is possible, so excess halogen can give a mixture. This is free radical substitution, not an addition reaction.

Why alkanes are unreactive. The C H bonds are strong, breaking them costs considerable energy. They are also relatively non polar, leaving no strongly charged site for a polar reagent to attack. Ultraviolet light changes the situation for a halogen by splitting its molecule into reactive radicals.

Crude oil fractions and exhaust. Heavy fractions have long molecules. Cracking supplies lower M r alkanes, useful as fuels, and alkenes, useful as chemical feedstocks. Engine combustion can release carbon monoxide, oxides of nitrogen and unburnt hydrocarbons. C O is poisonous because it reduces oxygen transport in blood, nitrogen oxides and unburnt hydrocarbons help form photochemical smog. Catalytic converters oxidise C O and hydrocarbons to C O two and H two O and reduce nitrogen oxides to N two, two C O plus two N O yields two C O two plus N two. This removes pollutants but still makes C O two.
Method.
Initiation, U V light causes homolytic fission, C L two yields two chlorine radical. Each chlorine atom takes one bonding electron.

Propagation, chlorine radical plus C two H six yields H C L plus C two H five radical, then C two H five radical plus C L two yields C two H five C L plus chlorine radical. A radical is regenerated, so the chain continues.
Termination, Two radicals join and no radical remains, for example C two H five radical plus chlorine radical yields C two H five C L or two C two H five radical yields C four H ten.
Worked example.

Suggest products when one molecule of decane cracks into octane and one other molecule. Carbon balance leaves two C atoms, hydrogen balance leaves four H atoms. The second product is ethene. C ten H twenty two yields C eight H eighteen plus C two H four. Octane is the lower M r alkane, ethene is the alkene. Count atoms on both sides before accepting the equation.
Worked example, cracking a different feedstock.
One molecule of C twelve H twenty six cracks into heptane and one alkene molecule.
Heptane is C seven H sixteen. Carbon remaining, twelve minus seven equals five.
Hydrogen remaining, twenty six minus sixteen equals ten, so the alkene is C five H ten.
Equation, C twelve H twenty six yields C seven H sixteen plus C five H ten. Check C, twelve equals seven plus five and H, twenty six equals sixteen plus ten.
Heptane is useful as a fuel, the pentene product can undergo addition polymerisation to make a polymer.
Your turn, complete the faded example.

One molecule of C fifteen H thirty two cracks into C nine H twenty and one alkene molecule. Carbon remaining, fifteen minus nine equals six. Complete the hydrogen subtraction, write the equation, check both elements, and state a use of the alkene.
Faded example answer.

Hydrogen remaining, thirty two minus twenty equals twelve. The equation is C fifteen H thirty two yields C nine H twenty plus C six H twelve. Check C, fifteen equals nine plus six and H, thirty two equals twenty plus twelve. The hexene product can be a monomer for addition polymerisation.
Traps.
Trap, Calling radical combination a propagation step. Why it's wrong, No radical is regenerated. Instead, Label it termination.
Trap, Assuming limited oxygen still gives only C O two. Why it's wrong, Carbon monoxide or soot can form. Instead, State the oxygen supply and balance the chosen products.
Trap, Saying a converter prevents all greenhouse gas release. Why it's wrong, Oxidation produces C O two. Instead, Name the pollutant removed and the product formed.
Exam technique.

For Describe, give reagents, conditions and products. For Explain alkane unreactivity, mention both C H bond strength and relative lack of polarity. For a mechanism, write complete initiation, propagation and termination equations with radical dots. For Suggest a cracking equation, balance C and H separately, a valid product pair is worth more than a named process alone.
